heading: Railway accident victims to get full compensation: Allahabad HC ends 90% fixed deposit rule
author: Edited by: Saurabh Thakur / TIMESOFINDIA.COM /  Sep 21, 2026, 14:57 IST
paragraphs: NEW DELHI: The Allahabad high court has directed the Railway Claims Tribunal (RCT) to release the entire compensation awarded to major claimants in railway accident cases, holding that keeping 90 percent of the amount in fixed deposits based on a claimant’s literacy or financial condition violates Article 14

The order was passed on September 10, 2026.Why did the claimants challenge the payment rules?According to the court order, the petitions were filed by families of passengers who died in railway accidents and by injured passengers who had received compensation from the RCT

The tribunal had released only 10 percent of the awarded amount and directed that the remaining 90 percent be kept in interest-bearing fixed deposits.The petitioners challenged Rule 5 of the Railway Accidents and Untoward Incidents (Compensation) Rules, 1990, particularly provisions allowing the tribunal to decide the mode of disbursement based on the claimant’s financial condition, literacy and other factors.The rule was introduced in 2020 following directions issued by the Delhi high court in Geeta Devi vs Union of India

The stated purpose was to protect claimants from exploitation by touts and middlemen.What did the high court find?Justice Rohit Ranjan Agarwal said the rules created a distinction between claimants based on literacy and financial position

It noted that the maximum compensation payable under Rule 3 of the 1990 Rules was Rs 8 lakh and questioned the justification for releasing only 10 percent, or Rs 80,000, while keeping Rs 7.20 lakh in a fixed deposit for three years.“Once a person with a weak financial condition is operating and managing his financial aspects, he cannot be restricted from using the awarded amount

There is no material on record to demonstrate that illiterate or financially weak person cannot manage the awarded amount,” the court noted.The court also examined the requirement that claimants open individual savings accounts in nationalised banks and face restrictions on cheque books and debit cards

It found such conditions excessive, saying the tribunal could require an account to be opened where a claimant did not already have one.The court said the rules could not be used to restrict the benefit granted under the Railways Act.“Once the Act provides for the compensation on account of untoward incident, it cannot through subordinate legislation like the Rules of 1990 curtail the benefit extended by the tribunal to a claimant in case of death of his near and dear one, or to a passenger sustaining injury,” the court added.The high court partly allowed the petitions and directed that Rule 5.1 and Rule 5.4.1(i) and (ii) be read down

Under the modified rule, the tribunal must release the awarded amount to major claimants, except those covered by the provision relating to minors or persons of unsound mind.The court also directed that amounts already kept in fixed deposits be immediately released.“The tribunal shall release the sum awarded to claimants pursuant to the award made therein except for claimants mentioned in Rule 5.2,” the court concluded.It further modified the orders passed by the RCT to the extent indicated in the judgment.
